purpose: Increment 7A designs ONE safe activation pass. It registers nothing and flips no status. Increments 8 and 9 build the components; Increment 7B performs the single atomic activation this file specifies.

sequencing_rule.statement: Component, backend authorization, tests and browser proof must all exist before a canonical status becomes `implemented`. The working-memory checklist's original Increment 7 ordering would have flipped statuses and run the generator before the four corrective pages existed, which the higher UI/UX authority forbids (UI/UX plan §7.2: a page is implemented only when a real component renders real data).
guarantees: no live route for a page that is not finished
no page marked implemented merely because its backend exists

host_scoping.problem_proved: The Super Administrator canonical path /audit (contract §5.4.18, Platform Audit) collides EXACTLY with the Merchant Audit account tree root /audit declared in resources/spa/src/router/routes/audit.ts. Both are authenticated account trees registered in one router today, so registering the canonical path globally would make one account's page shadow another's whole tree. This is measured from the router modules, not assumed.
host_scoping.additional_pressure: The canonical paths are host-relative by contract (navigation map header, ADR-016). /dashboard, /get-started, /account, /notifications and /reports are all names the seven remaining accounts will claim in UI-09 … UI-15, so a global registration would convert a single collision into seven.
host_scoping.decision: resources/spa/src/router/index.ts exports `createAppRouter(accountKey)`. Exactly ONE account tree is registered when the server resolved an account host; all eight are registered when no account context exists.
host_scoping.why_the_null_case_is_safe: When no account context is resolved, `requiresAccount` denies every account route unconditionally (guards.ts: `host === null` -> access-denied), so no account page can render and cross-account path shadowing is unreachable. The null composition exists so unit tests can assert route-name registration across all eight accounts exactly as they do today.
host_scoping.eager_creation_defect_closed: main.ts imports `router` at module scope, and ES module evaluation runs imports BEFORE `initAccountContext()` at line 14 — so a module-level `createRouter(...)` is built while the account context is still null. `createAppRouter` is therefore called FROM main.ts after `initAccountContext()`, which is the only ordering in which host scoping can be correct.
host_scoping.not_authorization: Host scoping selects the EXPERIENCE only (ADR-017). It is not a policy, gate or query scope input, and the backend remains the security boundary. Proven server-side by AccountHostDoesNotAuthorizeTest and re-proven in Increment 10.

tree_shape.why_the_parent_keeps_its_path: The canonical pages are absolute-path children, so the parent path is never part of their URL. It stays `/platform` for two measured reasons: `platform.landing` (the authenticated role landing, `path: ''`) is required by roleEntryRoutes.spec.ts via ROLE_ENTRY and is NOT one of the 160 contract pages; and a parent at `/` would contend with the UI-06 public landing `home`, which every account host serves at `/`.
tree_shape.child_paths: absolute (each begins with `/`), so vue-router resolves them at the host root while PlatformAdminLayout still wraps them. scripts/generate-ui07-navigation-contract.mjs already composes this correctly (`joinPath` returns an absolute child unchanged).
tree_shape.code_splitting: every canonical child uses a lazy `() => import(...)` component; no page is statically imported.

compatibility_redirects.loop_safe: target path differs from source; the redirect record has no child and no guard

deliberately_absent_redirects.reason: UI-07 removed this route because it rendered a Phase 4 stub. tests/e2e/ui-01-as-built-audit.spec.ts:179 records it as an absent destination and classifies whatever the browser produces. Introducing a redirect would rewrite that historical as-built finding. The canonical page is /dashboard; the old path remains a not-found, which is the truthful answer.

deliberately_absent_redirects.decision: NOT a redirect — it remains the authenticated role landing `platform.landing`
deliberately_absent_redirects.reason: It is a real rendered page (RoleLanding.vue), it is required by ROLE_ENTRY/roleEntryRoutes.spec.ts, and it is deliberately outside the 160-page count (navigation map `excluded_from_count`).

compatibility_rule: A compatibility redirect is never a navigation destination. The header registry resolves canonical route NAMES only; no redirect record carries a navigation label, and none is reachable from the shell.

new_backend_operations.itemised_justification: Directive §18.3 requires a real dashboard, and page-readiness §5.4.1 proves why a client-side aggregate is not acceptable: every platform read is a paginated list, so aggregating page 1 in the browser would misreport every count on a governance screen. This is the single approved UI-08 narrow read projection.
permitted_because: the governing data already exists (Phase 19, 20A, 20B, 20C, 20H tables)
the permission already exists (platform.merchant.view) — no new key
read-only: no mutation, no write path
new_backend_operations.gate_w_rule: Wallet, reconciliation and integration-health figures have no data source while External Gate W is closed. The projection returns them as an explicit unavailable state naming the gate — never a zero and never a healthy status.

no_other_new_operations: Get Started, Platform Audit and Account and Security are served entirely by shipped endpoints (see per-page api_operations below). No further operation is added, and no page is authorized to add a permission key.

permission_rule.statement: No remaining UI-08 page may add a permission key. Every page below cites a key that already exists in docs/auth/permission-matrix.yaml.

Five Phase 20B E2E cases drive its two tabs and its nested detail pane at /platform/registration-monitoring, and re-pointing them belongs to Increment 7B, where that path becomes a redirect — the same constraint, and the same resolution, as billing-settings in 9C. pages.browser_proof_prerequisite: no impersonation, no first-admin creation, no merchant operation; foreign ULID does not enumerate
pages.not_primary_navigation_reason: Record detail route addressed by a public ULID; it has no parameter-free primary navigation destination. The UI-07 generator rejects a parameterised primary-navigation target, so this stays `detail_route` and is reached from the directory.
pages.api_operations_amendment_reason: 7A listed platform.audit-logs.index for a per-merchant governance timeline. Measured against the shipped read it cannot supply one: PlatformAuditLogController::index returns the platform chain (merchant_id IS NULL) and AuditLogIndexRequest allowlists action, severity, actor, branch, subject_type, dates, sort and per_page — there is no merchant or subject-identity filter, and its SUBJECT_TYPES allowlist does not include Merchant. Client-side narrowing of one page of results would render a PARTIAL timeline as if it were complete, which is the failure mode the readiness matrix already recorded as a measured gap for this page. The page therefore names the timeline as unavailable, with the reason, and links to the platform audit surface for anyone holding platform.audit.view. No new operation, filter, permission or migration was added: OpenAPI stays at 336.
